result:
Done. The newsletter sign-up lives entirely under `modules/newsletter/` and every check in the definition of done passes.

**Verification results**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `bun run typecheck` | passes |
| `bun test` | 9 pass, 0 fail (7 new newsletter tests) |
| `bunx guren check` | 18 passed, 4 pre-existing warnings, 0 failures |
| `bunx guren check --arch` | 2 passed, 0 failures |
| Arch check with probe files under `app/` and `routes/` | both reported as `[fail]`, then probes removed |
| `bun run lint` | clean |

**How the endpoints behave**

- **Subscribe** validates the body at the route level with a zod email schema, so a bad or empty address answers a JSON 422 with the error under `email` before the database is touched. A duplicate address raises a ValidationException with the same shape. A new row gets a 40-character URL-safe token and a null `confirmed_at`, then the visitor is sent back to the Referer when it is on-site, otherwise to `/`.
- **Confirm** looks the token up, aborts with 404 when unknown, otherwise stamps `confirmed_at` and redirects to `/`.
- **Unsubscribe** deletes the row for that address and redirects back the same way.

**One judgment call to flag.** Addresses are trimmed and lower-cased before storage and lookup, so `Foo@Example.com` and `foo@example.com` count as the same subscriber. The contract says capitalisation is not checked, so this only affects what marketing sees in the table.

**Summary of changes.** I scaffolded the module with `bunx guren make:module newsletter`, which registered `newsletterModule` in `src/app.ts` and added the schema re-export to the root `db/schema.ts`. Under `modules/newsletter/` I wrote the table in `db/schema.ts`, the model in `app/Models/NewsletterSubscription.ts` with only `email` fillable, the validator in `app/Http/Validators/NewsletterValidator.ts`, the controller in `app/Http/Controllers/NewsletterController.ts`, the three routes in `routes.ts`, and feature tests in `tests/NewsletterController.test.ts`. I generated the migration `db/migrations/20260925064150_newsletter_subscriptions/` with the project's migrate tooling, ran codegen so the generated route types include the new routes, added `modules/**/*` to `tsconfig.json` so module code is typechecked, and created `guren.arch.ts` at the project root with a rule that fails the arch check whenever any file under `app/` or `routes/` imports from `modules/newsletter/`, including type-only imports. Nothing under `app/` or `routes/` was changed.
